attribution: Achievement data from Steam (Steam Web API, app 203140)
StrategyWiki: no usable walkthrough, nothing used — https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Hitman:_Absolution
Fandom (hitman.fandom.com, CC BY-SA): page names only were checked to confirm structure; no text copied — https://hitman.fandom.com/wiki/Hitman:_Absolution
notes: Backlog game, all-AAA pass: picked from RAWG's most-added list for its year across all genres (docs/PLAN.md section 2, genre filter widened 2026-10-23). RAWG's first result is the expected entry (id 5583); RAWG keeps "Hitman: Absolution - Elite Edition", "Hitman: Sniper Challenge" and "Hitman HD Enhanced Collection" as separate additions. Steam app 203140 ("Hitman: Absolution™" in the store list; its schema is named "ValveTestApp203140", a placeholder) was used. StrategyWiki has "Hitman: Absolution" as a stub at completion stage 0 (in Category:Stubs): only the Table of Contents is written; Controls, Gameplay and Walkthrough are linked but not written. hitman.fandom.com answers the API under "Hitman: Absolution" with about 245 linked articles; names only were looked at, nothing copied. 20 of 47 Steam achievements are hidden: NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_3_4 to 3_23 in an unbroken run, falling mostly steadily from 84.8% to 32.7%, so they look like story milestones; they are split ten and ten by API number, our own choice. Two are much rarer than their neighbours, "Not Worth It" (14.4%) and "Faith Can Move Mountains" (22.6%), and may be optional feats rather than plain story beats. "Self-improvement" (bought a weapon upgrade) sits next to the Contracts dollars achievement in the list, but the data does not tie it to Contracts, so it is in techniques.
